question: Does the identity key sign a statement that names the anchor account or domain?
Does the anchor account or domain publish content that names the key or identifier?
Does a party other than the key holder and the anchor platform sign the binding?
Does creating the link require an OAuth or OIDC login to the anchor?
Is the link expressed as a delegation of authority (a capability), not a claim of sameness?
Is a DNS name or web domain a supported anchor?
Is an email address a supported anchor?
Is a centralized social or developer platform (GitHub, X, Mastodon, Reddit) a supported anchor?
Can a verifier check the link from presented data alone, with no network fetch?
Must the verifier fetch from the anchor platform or domain?
Must the verifier trust the key of a third-party issuer?
Must the verifier query a registry, directory, log, or chain?
Can a verifier check the link without any service run by the authors of the offering?
Does verification stop working if the anchor platform closes its public API or blocks scraping?
Do existing links stay valid after the identity key rotates?
Is there a defined mechanism to revoke a link, other than deleting the published proof?
Do links or proofs expire by design?
Is recovery after loss of the identity key defined?
Do timestamps, nonces, expiry, or a log stop an old proof from being replayed after the anchor changes owner?
Is the link or the identity record kept in an append-only transparency log?
Can the user host the identity record or proof without any third-party operator?
Is the identity record replicated across several independent operators?
Can the mechanism anchor a generic DID or a raw ed25519 key, not only its own key type?
Can new anchor platforms be added without a spec change?
Ordinal: 0 vendor-only or none, 1 draft or proposal, 2 community spec (NIP, WG, DIF), 3 formal standard (W3C Rec, IETF RFC).
Was the offering maintained or changed in 2025 or 2026?
Does at least one widely used client display the verified link?
Can the mechanism be added to a key system that I already own (attach tier)?
Does getting the link require adopting the identity system of the offering (migrate tier)?
